conventions.convention: Chain-label words are read downward from the upper endpoint. Labels may depend on the already traversed upper root. Condition (N) requires pairwise distinct labels on each maximal chain of every rooted interval; condition (L) requires a unique strictly increasing, lexicographically first chain there. Empty and one-entry words are vacuously increasing and falling.

Congruence classes have least and greatest members, not merely minimal and maximal members. The interval criterion assumes classes already are closed intervals and requires both endpoint maps to be order-preserving.

Davis cells are indexed by left cosets wW_T ordered by inclusion. The empty spherical type indexes vertices; it is distinct from the formal empty face subsequently adjoined to the gluing poset. The finite spherical Coxeter complex instead uses proper parabolic cosets with reverse incidence.

A single positive tuple d_s specifies all Coxeter cells, with B(x_T,e_s)=d_s. Face metrics use affine isometries and compatible orthogonal projections. Equal distances give regular dihedral polygons and Euclidean cubes; arbitrary positive distances need not do so.

Cell coordinates use the unique minimum-length coset representative dot(q). A point coordinate in the chamber face w_0 C_I has stabilizer (dot(q) w_0) W_I (dot(q) w_0)^−1; it need not have stabilizer obtained merely by testing its untransported simple-root pairings.

The coarse Davis vertex link is the nerve with prescribed edge lengths π−π/m(s,t), rather than π/m(s,t); the simplicial order-complex vertex link is its barycentric subdivision. Angular metrics truncate componentwise intrinsic distances at π, including infinite distances between components. Prescribed cell lengths are distinguished from global shortest-path distances.

The general complete-CAT(0) circumcenter branch assumes AC to select a minimizing sequence. Its proper-space branch is choice-free. The Davis CAT(0) and finite-subgroup theorems explicitly assume AC through their geometric suppliers.

load_bearing.statement: For a Coxeter matrix with S finite and the compatible Coxeter cells, the spherical-coset cellulation is a connected, locally finite isometric polyhedral gluing with finitely many shapes. Its chain metric is complete and proper and induces the weak topology; its barycentric subdivision is the Davis realization. Cells wW_T have dimension |T| and setwise stabilizer wW_Tw^−1. Each point has a unique carrier cell and the stated chamber-coordinate spherical-parabolic stabilizer. The cellular action is isometric and proper, its quotient is homeomorphic to K, and U(W,K) is equivariantly homeomorphic to the realization.

For spherical T and positive d_s, C_T=conv(W_T x_T) is a |T|-dimensional compact convex polyhedral cell containing 0 in its interior, with faces indexed uniquely by parabolic cosets and inclusion preserved. For U⊆T, the orthogonal projection of x_T onto V_U is x_U; its complementary vector is W_U-fixed. The stated affine maps identify C_U isometrically with its indexed faces and satisfy the stated cocycle for U⊆T⊆T′.

Assuming AC, for finite S and any positive tuple d_s, the Davis angular vertex link is canonically isometric to the nerve with spherical Gram matrices B_T and prescribed edges π−π/m(s,t). It is finite large metric flag. The cell link at wW_U is the spherical face link at U, with normalized Schur-complement Gram matrices; every such link is finite large metric flag and CAT(1) for its truncated angular metric.

Assuming AC, the Davis complex of a finite-rank Coxeter system, with the chain metric for any fixed positive tuple d_s, has CAT(1) cell links, is locally CAT(0), and is a connected proper complete geodesic length space. It is simply connected and globally CAT(0), with unique minimizing geodesics and the continuous geodesic contraction satisfying d(H_t(x),H_t(y))≤t d(x,y); in particular it is contractible.

For a nonempty bounded subset Y of a complete CAT(0) space, assuming AC, the finite radius function attains its infimum at a unique center. Isometries preserving Y fix the center. Common fixed sets are closed and convex, and when nonempty are CAT(0) and contractible; they are complete if the ambient space is complete. A bounded orbit gives a fixed point. In a proper CAT(0) space these conclusions hold without Choice.

For an interval in a finite graded poset with a descending rooted-chain labeling satisfying (N) and (L) on every rooted interval, lexicographically earlier and later maximal chains admit the stated codimension-one earlier replacement containing their intersection. Lexicographic order, with arbitrary tie-breaking, shells both the closed- and open-interval order complexes. In every rooted interval, μ(v,w)=(-1)^ρ(v,w) times the number of strictly falling maximal chains, with the stated rank-zero and rank-one conventions.

Let L be a finite lattice and θ an equivalence relation whose classes are intervals with endpoints in the class. Then θ is a lattice congruence if and only if its lower and upper endpoint maps are order-preserving.

seams_checked.note: Coset-calculus F3 quotes W_I∩W_J=W_(I∩J) exactly. Standard-parabolic and minimum-representative uses retain their left/right conventions and finite-rank domains.
Orbit-face and stabilizer arguments apply the chamber theorem only to finite-type systems, including spherical subsystems. Proper-coset incidence reversal and rank-zero conventions are preserved.

The Davis cellulation verifies cocycle and intersection conditions, connectedness, local finiteness and finite shapes before invoking subdivision, topology, properness and completeness. It does not infer global cell-distance equality from face isometries.

The link lemma states the finite large metric flag supplier with AC and the truncated angular metric. It checks the positive-definite clique criterion and applies CAT(1) to vertex and face links without replacing prescribed edge lengths by global distances.
